result.title: SwitchSplat: Learning Discrete Object States from Casually Captured Scenes
result.comment: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (Conference Papers). 19 pages, 15 figures, 8 tables. Project page: https://switchsplat.github.io
result.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting has made high-fidelity 3D reconstruction fast and accessible, yet existing representations assume a static world. This assumption breaks down in casual captures, where a user naturally interacts with the environment -- opening doors, toggling switches, or moving objects -- introducing discrete state changes that no current framework can model. Time-conditioned dynamic methods such as 4DGS conflate when a state was observed with what state the scene is in, limiting them to replaying seen sequences rather than composing arbitrary object configurations. We present SwitchSplat, the first 3DGS representation to address this gap via a base+slot decomposition: a shared static base captures the invariant scene, while each slot independently holds the two binary states (on/off) of one interactable object. Because the assignment of Gaussians to slots is fully differentiable, the model discovers the geometry of each state directly from video, without manual annotation. At inference, the user can freely combine slot states and render the resulting scene from any viewpoint. We validate SwitchSplat on a new casual-capture dataset and show that it outperforms static and dynamic baselines in novel-view synthesis quality, while uniquely supporting rendering of state combinations never seen during capture. Project page: https://switchsplat.github.io

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SwitchSplat，用「共享静态 base + 每物体槽位」的可微分解把随手拍摄场景中的二值离散状态（开/关）显式建模为可自由组合的槽位，从而支持从未见过的状态组合下的新视角渲染。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「时间戳与真实状态解耦」「离散槽位状态及其可微分配」可能对 latent 状态定义、视觉证据筛选与未见状态组合的泛化提供概念类比，可核查是否可迁移到多 latent 假设的组合与贡献分配。
